summary: Formalizes a non-destructive WebP working-copy scan pipeline (issue #200). Each receipt keeps its own top-level path/sha256/source_url untouched (the true Oracle-of-the-Void master's identity, restorable via the existing download_oracle_printings.py/download_expansion_printings.py any time). A new sibling working_copy field records a matching WebP artifact from the 'Catalogue artwork - WebP 85 - v1' Release instead (matched by the original's own sha256). New tool tools/content/sync_webp_working_copies.py auto-fetches/extracts the release into a local gitignored cache (pinned zip sha256, verified before extracting) and materializes each matching WebP locally -- no session has to manually rediscover the release again. build_definition_fields (shared by every package_*_wave.py script) now prefers a receipt's working_copy when present, falling back to the original untouched. Ran --apply for real: 2,485 of 2,952 receipts now carry a working copy (~85% smaller on disk); those receipt updates are committed this time since they never overwrite the original identity (unlike issue #198's own destructive audit_and_install_scans.py, which is superseded).
validation: python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/content -> 116/116 (9 new tests: 3 in test_package_vanilla_wave.py covering working-copy preference/fallback/tamper-rejection, 6 in new test_sync_webp_working_copies.py covering apply/dry-run/unmatched/idempotence/pinned-hash-rejection/cache-reuse); python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/collaboration -> 43/43. Ran the real sync against the actual repo (not just tests): 2,485/2,952 receipts updated, spot-checked one real published card (oracle-l5r-10099) through build_definition_fields end-to-end -- correctly read the WebP working copy and wrote a valid re-encoded JPEG -- then reverted that incidental Content/Published/*.jpg change (this PR's scope is the pipeline/receipts, not re-encoding already-shipped published art; that's a separate product decision the user did not ask for this pass). No C# touched, so no dotnet checks run.
remaining: 467 of 2,952 receipts have no WebP counterpart in the release and still need their true original restored the old way (re-running download_oracle_printings.py/download_expansion_printings.py) if a future wave needs one of them. Whether to also retroactively re-encode the ~198 already-shipped src/L5R.Client/Content/Published/*.jpg files from their WebP working copies (further storage savings on the actually-committed client assets, not just the local dev cache) is an open product question, not actioned here.
